newsitem.title: USA: Callon cites higher production for gains.
newsitem.headline: Callon cites higher production for gains.

text.p: Callon Petroleum Co said Wednesday reported with record increases in net income, production and revenues during the first quarter.

"Although prices for both oil and natural gas improved in the first quarter of 1997, higher production was the primary reason for the substantial improvement in revenues," chief executive Fred L. Callon said.

"More than 85 percent of the $6.1 million boost in revenues is due to increased production with this increase primarily attributable to drilling operations in our Shallow Miocene focus area during the fourth quarter of 1996."

Due to the existing field infrastructure within the Shallow Miocene focus area, operating costs, on a unit of production basis, decreased by 25 percent, further increasing the company's profit margin, he added.
Net income during the first quarter of 1997 was $3.7 million, or $0.47 per share, compared to $1.4 million, or $0.12 per share, during the first quarter of 1996.
Revenues were $12.8 million compared to $6.5 million for the same period of 1996, the company said.

During this same period, earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization increased by more than 145 percent to $9.5 million compared to $3.9 million in the same period of 1996. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
